articles.title: Magnesium is essential for health. But can supplements really help with digestion, muscle pain, anxiety and sleep? | Antiviral
articles.summary: Experts cite inconsistent evidence for supplementing with the essential mineral – and warn taking magnesium without a deficiency has risks. Dietitian Danielle Shine says her Instagram inbox was filled with questions after actor Scarlett Johansson was quoted in the Daily Mail and other publications…
body: “I know that everybody is taking magnesium now. It’s so helpful,” Johansson reportedly told beauty publication Byrdie.
Shine says celebrity endorsement of supplements is persuasive and always leads to an uptick in questions.
“The general sentiment was, ‘If she [Johansson] takes magnesium and says it works for her, then maybe I should be taking it too,’” Shine says.

Magnesium is an essential mineral that the body needs for blood pressure regulation, bone health and many other important functions. Because the body doesn’t produce it, diet is critical, with nuts, seeds, legumes, leafy greens and brown rice among good sources.

articles.title: Inside Seoul’s K-beauty ‘mecca’: I hunted for the best skincare at the world’s biggest Korean beauty store
articles.summary: What’s actually worth buying at Olive Young? A dispatch from the epicenter of Korean beauty, including the best skincare, face masks and hair care. Five of the best Korean skincare brands you can actually find in the US.
body: If flying all the way to Seoul into the eye of the storm for some face masks sounds like overkill, I have good news for the skincare lover reading this. More and more Americans are getting access to Korea’s largest health and beauty retailer, which opened its first US stor e in Pasadena earlier this year with a line that stretched a quarter-mile long. Last month, it made a buzzy debut in Sephora, where shoppers can buy 19 curated Korean brands in hundreds of locations nationwide. It’s been a relief for K-beauty fans in the US who have been stuck with the frustrating reality that the best stuff isn’t FDA-approved for sale here, or they can only find marked-up or counterfeit options on Amazon.

For the brick-and-mortar averse, I have more good news: Olive Young also opened online shipping for the US this year. Just as you would in its stores in Korea, you’ll find a dizzying array of brands on its site: familiar names such as Biodance and Abib, but also domestically popular ones that many Americans haven’t heard of yet, including Hanyul and Ilso.
points: A dispatch from the epicenter of Korean beauty, including the best skincare, face masks and hair care.

articles.title: M&S links up with Sephora to lure younger shoppers
articles.summary: Beauty specialist will open branded areas in 100 Marks & Spencer stores and will sell its products on chain’s website. Business live – latest updates. Marks & Spencer has signed a deal with Sephora to open areas under the beauty brand’s name within its stores, in its latest tactic to attract…
body: The French retailer is to launch branded areas staffed by Sephora employees in 100 M&S stores and sell through the British retailer’s website in spring next year.

Sephora relaunched in the UK in 2023 with huge fanfare and now has about 18 stand-alone British stores. The company is owned by LVMH, the luxury goods group led by Bernard Arnault, who with his family is among the world’s richest people with a $171bn (£129bn) fortune, according to Forbes.

The company has rapidly expanded on its second attempt to enter the UK market after closing a handful of stores in 2005, having failed make a dent in a competitive sector. The deal with M&S marks a new strategy in its expansion plans.

Analysts have said Sephora’s work with up-and-coming brands and collaborations with high-profile influencers on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube has helped the company reach its target female audience of 24- to 36-year-olds.

articles.title: Why are garlic presses so out of fashion? | Kitchen aide
articles.summary: It’s the gadget people love to hate – but maybe it does have a place in the kitchen? Why are garlic presses suddenly a no-no? Recipes now stipulate grating instead, but who wants lumps of garlic in their dinner?
body: Christina Soteriou, recipe writer at Ottolenghi Inc and author of Big Veg Energy, however, takes a more balanced approach: “A garlic press is not necessarily a no-no, and there can definitely be a time and a place for it,” she says. “It’s definitely quicker [than chopping], but I’d use it only when said garlic is going into a sauce, stew or braise.” Which is to say, in a dish where those lumps that concern Sally will cook down and dissolve almost entirely.

As with most things in life, Sally should just do her, though Soteriou does suggest sticking to one rule: “A garlic press for anything that’s going to be slow-cooked, and a Microplane, pestle and mortar, or minced for anything where it will be raw or cooked very quickly.” Just “never, ever buy ready-crushed garlic”, Chandler says. “That’s another business altogether and it tastes awful.”

articles.title: H&M, Inditex, Bestseller and Adidas Back Coalition
articles.summary: After campaigning for extended producer responsibility fees to follow the flow of used clothing for five years, The Or Foundation — and its new brand partners — will put its theory to the test.
body: Last year, while reporting our (Re)Made in Ghana series, I stood on the beach in Accra, Ghana, and witnessed the destruction caused by used clothing exports up close. I walked over the mountains of used clothing clogging the sand; wrestled with the tangled tentacles of waste to unearth individual items and register individual brand labels; and watched as local volunteers took pickaxes to those with deeper roots.

The Tide Turners cooperative, supported by US Ghanaian non-profit The Or Foundation, runs these weekly beach clean-ups. But their efforts to tackle a textile waste crisis they did nothing to create go unnoticed — and uncompensated — despite the EU’s progress toward extended producer responsibility (EPR) regulations that would make the polluter pay for cleaning up its own waste.
points: After campaigning for extended producer responsibility fees to follow the flow of used clothing for five years, The Or Foundation — and its new brand partners — will put its theory to the test.

articles.title: An Exclusive Look Inside Dolly Parton’s New Museum in Nashville
articles.summary: Dolly’s Life of Many Colors Museum, on the third floor of her SongTeller Hotel in downtown Nashville, features the largest exhibition of Dolly Parton’s personal effects anywhere—including the dress she wore to marry Carl Dean in 1966.
body: As a little girl growing up in Tennessee, Rebecca Seaver’s playground was a fashion lover’s dream. During visits to her aunt Dolly’s house, she’d head straight for the closet—her favorite room—and marvel at the sea of sequins, rhinestones, beaded trims, and rows and rows of high heels before her.

Decades later, in her capacity as director of the Dolly Parton Archive (the official archive dedicated to preserving Parton’s legacy), Seaver often returned to that closet. Among the things she discovered there was a small, worn military trunk belonging to Parton’s husband, Carl Dean, from his time in the National Guard.
Though Seaver didn’t think much of the trunk when she first brought it back to the archive, in 2024, her archive manager was sorting through the storage when Seaver heard her let out a scream.

“I was sitting at my desk, and I thought it must be a mouse or a bug, but when I ran back there to see what was going on, she had a dress laid out on her lap.” For years, Parton’s wedding dress was presumed to be lost. But suddenly, there it was: a simple white A-line garment in a trunk full of photos and other mementos, perfectly frozen in time from 1966.

articles.title: Inside Dove Cameron and Damiano David’s Timeless Wedding at a Medieval Tuscan Estate
articles.summary: Exclusive: Dove Cameron wore a custom Valentino gown with a star-embroidered veil to marry former Måneskin frontman Damiano David in the hilltop village resort of Castiglion del Bosco in Tuscany. See all the photos here.
body: Dove Cameron and Damiano David’s continent-spanning love story began as you might expect for a pair of popular musicians: they briefly crossed paths backstage at an awards show. To be precise, the 2022 MTV Video Music Awards, where Dove received the Best New Artist accolade—a prize for which Måneskin, the Italian rock group fronted by Damiano that is currently on hiatus, were also nominated. “The band congratulated me on winning the award, but Damiano barely spoke two words to me!” Dove recalls. “I talked briefly to his bandmates, then went on with my night.”

As fate would have it, they were reunited at the same awards show the following year. “It wasn’t until the following year that we really had a reason to speak—he approached me about a song we had worked on virtually a few months ago,” Dove continues. “At that point, we were both single, and his energy towards me had completely changed. He invited me to see Måneskin’s show at Madison Square Garden, and later that night, the after-party.” Their romance blossomed immediately: “Everything moved pretty quickly from there,” Dove notes.

articles.title: Spotify and Claude Are Both Down
articles.summary: If you're having trouble getting your Spotify playlists up and running this morning, you're not alone. The music streaming platform is currently down for tens of thousands of users, at least. Downdetector is showing roughly 40,000 reports since 9:31 a.m.
body: Curiously, Spotify's outage comes at the same time as an outage with Claude, the AI platform from Anthropic. Downdetector shows tens of thousands of user reports here as well, and Anthropic confirmed an ongoing issue with Claude: "We are investigating reports of degraded performance affecting claude.ai, platform.claude.com, the Claude API, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork. We will provide an update as soon as possible."

It's not clear why these services are down this morning, or if they are related. But in all likelihood, Spotify and Anthropic will get their platforms back up and running soon. Typically, these occasional outages are resolved in hours, if not minutes, barring a widespread problem, like an outage with a cloud hosting provider. Last year's AWS outage "broke the internet," as did November's Cloudflare outage. There's no reason to think that's the case with these outages at this time.

articles.summary: The Vogue Book Club event will also include a live taping of “The Run-Through” podcast with Chloe Malle and Daisy Edgar-Jones.
body: We’ve swooned over Emerald Fennell’s Wuthering Heights, girded our loins for The Devil Wears Prada 2, and now it’s time to shift into Jane Austen mode for the Vogue Book Club ’s upcoming screening of the new Sense and Sensibility.

Austen’s debut novel, which was first published anonymously in 1811, delves deep into the romantic entanglements (or, dare we say it, Georgian-era situationships?) of the Dashwood sisters after their father’s death. Vogue ’s special advance screening of Georgia Oakley’s new adaptation will take place on October 14 in New York, and include both a showing of the film and a live taping of The Run-Through podcast, featuring Vogue US’s head of editorial content, Chloe Malle, and Sense and Sensibility star Daisy Edgar-Jones.
